# Summary of Studienstiftung
The Studienstiftung des deutschen Volkes is Germany’s largest and oldest scholarship foundation, initially founded in 1925, re-established in 1948, and dedicated to supporting exceptionally talented students and doctoral candidates across all disciplines. It offers both financial support—including monthly allowances (approx. €300 for undergraduates, €1,550 for PhD students as of 2025), subsidies for health insurance, and need-based scholarships—and academic support such as summer schools, research groups, mentoring by academic liaison professors, workshops, and language courses. Scholar selection emphasizes academic excellence, initiative, and social commitment, with admission through nominations by schools, professors, examination boards, competition winners, alumni, or via an assessment test. As of 2023, the foundation admitted approximately 2,179 undergraduate/graduate and 301 doctoral scholars annually, with diverse selection rates based on nomination type.
The foundation also runs internal and open scholarship programs in collaboration with external partners, e.g., KAUST internships for STEM students and musical residencies with the Beethoven House. It supports scholars’ own initiatives through funding for events and conferences, and promotes inclusive community-building, exemplified by subsidizing annual queer scholars' meetings since 2014. The Studienstiftung has a notable roster of alumni across natural sciences, social sciences, politics, business, arts, and journalism, including Nobel laureates, Leibniz and Fields medalists, and prominent public figures. Scholarships are non-taxable and can include funding for study-abroad components.
